questions.question: How often should you inspect cargo while transporting it?

options.text: Only at the start of the trip.
Only after driving a long distance.
After every break.

questions.explanation: Check your cargo and securing devices before you start. While driving, check them within the first 50 miles, every 3 hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: What should you do when using a fire extinguisher?

options.text: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
Aim at the flames.
Use any extinguisher on any type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
questions.explanation: Stay far from the fire and aim at the base, not the flames. Different fires need different treatments. If you are unsure, wait for trained firefighters.

questions.question: What is the safest speed to drive in heavy traffic?

options.text: Slower than other vehicles.
The same speed as other vehicles.
Faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as surrounding vehicles. If two vehicles travel at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot collide.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: Stop cargo from moving.
Keep cargo from being loaded too high.
Keep cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, and/or to the sides of cargo to prevent it from sliding during movement.

questions.question: How should you load a trailer?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
Do not worry about how weight is spread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distribute weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance your load carefully. Too much weight on an axle can damage it and hurt steering. Too little weight reduces traction and makes handling harder.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes during the driving test?

options.text: Ignore other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from the body?

options.text: By exercising.
At a fixed rate.
More quickly if you stay awake.

questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a steady rate. Coffee and cold showers do not speed this up. The only way to sober up is to give your body time.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire fails?

options.text: Use the brakes.
Stay off the brakes.
Swerve.

questions.explanation: Braking after a tire failure can cause you to lose control. Avoid the brakes until your vehicle slows down.

questions.question: What happens if you get a second conviction for driving a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher?

options.text: You lose your CDL for life.
You lose your CDL for five years.
You lose your CDL for one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose your CDL for life.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher. A first offense results in losing your CDL for one year. A second offense results in losing your CDL for life.

questions.question: How should you adjust your mirrors before a trip?

options.text: Your vehicle should not be visible in any mirror.
Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: When mirrors are adjusted correctly, you can see part of your vehicle. This gives you a reference point to judge where other objects are.

questions.question: When turning, drivers usually look:

options.text: In the direction they are turning.
In the opposite direction of the turn.
Behind their vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction they are turning.
questions.explanation: Drivers look in the direction they are turning. Even without a signal, a driver's body movements can show they plan to turn.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts should be:

options.text: Repaired immediately.
Repaired later.
Left alone because they cannot be identified.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed right away.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirrors.
Use both side mirrors.
Never ask for help from another person.

questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both mirrors often when backing. Ask a helper to assist whenever possible.

questions.question: To avoid aggressive driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster.
Make gestures at other drivers.
Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, give other drivers the benefit of the doubt. Assume they have valid reasons for what they do and do not take their actions personally.

questions.question: Items on a flatbed trailer must be:

options.text: Heavy enough that they don't need to be strapped down.
Left unsecured when driving under 35 mph.
Always secured.

questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must always be tied down to prevent it from moving or falling off.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, you should:

options.text: Ignore it and keep driving.
Hope the vehicle lasts until another driver takes over.
Stop and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: Use your senses while driving to find mechanical problems. If you see, hear, smell, or feel something wrong, stop and check it out.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage rate during a test is ____ per minute.

options.text: 2 psi
4 psi
6 psi

questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi of air per minute during a test.

questions.question: People working on a broken-down vehicle may:

options.text: Be aware of traffic.
Be focused on repairs and not notice nearby traffic.
Not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be focused on repairs and not notice nearby traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a disabled vehicle. They may be focused on the repair and not paying attention to traffic.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. Both systems share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard for the driver to see behind the trailer.
Extra weight may be in the front of the vehicle.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
Trailers cannot be driven in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard for the driver to see behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only back up if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: What should a driver do if a vehicle starts to hydroplane?

options.text: Speed up.
Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.
Push in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch to regain control.

questions.question: What vehicle should you use for a driving test?

options.text: The same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
Any vehicle, even if it is different from the type you will drive with your CDL.
A vehicle supplied by the testing station.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the same type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are responsible for providing the vehicle.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?

options.text: Coffee
Exercise
Time

questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a set rate that cannot be sped up. Coffee and exercise do not help. Only time allows your body to process and remove alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Take a stimulant pill.
Stop and rest.
Keep driving.

questions.explanation: Stop driving and get sleep if you feel tired. Continuing to drive when tired is dangerous and can cause crashes. Pills may keep you awake briefly but will not make you alert.

questions.question: When should you use placards?

options.text: Whenever a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
Only when there is extra space on the truck.
Only when hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be displayed whenever a vehicle carries hazardous materials. They must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: Puts the cargo in a large box.
Stops cargo from sliding during transport.
Prevents others from buying the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing keep cargo from moving during transport.

questions.question: What color light shows the ABS is not working?

options.text: Green
Blue
Yellow

questions.explanation: A yellow warning light tells the driver that the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?

options.text: Can damage vehicle parts.
Is needed to warm up vehicle parts.
Improves fuel efficiency.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually to avoid jerking. Rough acceleration can damage the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.
The maximum weight a vehicle can pull.
The minimum weight a vehicle can haul.

questions.correctAnswerText: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: The GVWR is the loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: How do you make your vehicle more visible during the day?

options.text: Use your low beam headlights.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your clearance lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights for the best visibility during the day. High beam headlights can be dangerous around other drivers.

questions.question: When it is hard to see other vehicles at dawn or dusk, you should:

options.text: Keep your lights off.
Turn your lights on.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.explanation: Use your headlights on low beam at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?

options.text: A loud sound
Vibration
Smoother steering

questions.explanation: Signs of tire failure include a loud bang, heavy thumping, or vibration. If steering feels heavy or the rear slides, stop and check your tires.

questions.question: To know if your vehicle can handle a load, you must know:

options.text: The vehicle's suspension rating.
The tire rating for the front tires only.
The tire rating for the rear tires only.

questions.explanation: You must know your vehicle's suspension weight capacity. It is your job to make sure you do not overload your vehicle.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.
Get some coffee.
Drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop and sleep when you feel tired. Do not try to push on to your destination. Caffeine is not a safe solution.

questions.question: When you check your windshield wiper blades, they should be:

options.text: Loose.
Sticky.
Secure.

questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage and make sure they are fastened tightly.

questions.question: In icy conditions, a retarder should be:

options.text: Turned on.
Turned off.
Only used on the rear wheels.

questions.explanation: Turn off the retarder on icy roads. It can cause your vehicle to skid when there is poor traction.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the safe limit, you should:

options.text: Continue to drive.
Pull over and figure out what's wrong.
Run the air conditioner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and figure out what's wrong.
questions.explanation: Stop driving right away. High coolant temperature means something is wrong with your vehicle. It could cause engine failure or a fire.

questions.question: Rolling backward when you start to accelerate is dangerous because:

options.text: The transmission may be damaged.
The truck is not made to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can move forward without rolling back. Rolling backward can cause you to hit another vehicle or object behind you.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, the parking brake is applied by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.
Pushing a yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pulling a yellow, diamond-shaped knob.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob to apply the parking brake. Push it in to release it.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, you must:

options.text: The State will inform your employer.
Tell your employer.
Tell the shipper.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also tell your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. Parking tickets do not count.

questions.question: When are containerized loads used?

options.text: When cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
When cargo has been or will be transported by train.
When cargo is a liquid.

questions.correctAnswerText: When cargo has been or will be transported by train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight travels part of the way by rail or ship. Sealed containers cannot be inspected, but drivers must make sure containers do not exceed safe weight limits.

questions.question: If you brake on dry pavement at 55 mph, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
45 feet
20 feet

questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, when must you tell your employer?

options.text: Within three hours.
Within one week.
Within 30 days.

questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also tell your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To keep cargo in a large box.
To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
To stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: What should you do if confronted by an aggressive driver?

options.text: Make eye contact to communicate with them.
Ignore their gestures.
Do not move out of their path.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as this may provoke them. Do not let them provoke you.

questions.question: What should you do before driving downhill?

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.
Shift into a lower gear.
Move into the left lane.

questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before going downhill. This reduces wear on your brakes.

questions.question: When making a left turn with two turn lanes, why should you start in the rightmost lane?

options.text: You can see other turning vehicles on your left better than on your right.
Your vehicle will turn more quickly.
Other vehicles will move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see other turning vehicles on your left better than on your right.
questions.explanation: When making a left turn with multiple lanes, start in the rightmost lane. Large vehicles often swing right to turn left. It is safer to have other left-turning traffic to your left instead of your right. This gives you a better view of other turning vehicles and reduces collision risk.

questions.question: Which vehicles have the most trouble with strong winds?

options.text: Lighter vehicles.
Heavier vehicles.
Flatbed trailers.

questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. This is especially true for drivers of lighter commercial vehicles.

questions.question: After changing a tire and driving a short distance, what should you check?

options.text: That the lug nuts are still tight.
That the tire is wearing evenly.
That the tire air pressure is correct.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the lug nuts are still tight.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance on a newly changed tire, stop and check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: How much alcohol can your liver process per hour?

options.text: One alcoholic drink
Two alcoholic drinks
Three alcoholic drinks

questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the higher your blood alcohol level becomes. Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate of about one drink per hour.
